# Results — Study 815 (Variance-Ratio Reversal)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Lo &
MacKinlay (1988): the **variance ratio** `VR(q) = Var(q-day return) / (q × Var(1-day
return))` diagnoses a random-walk departure — `VR < 1` mean-reverting, `VR > 1` trending —
and a long-low-VR (mean-reverting) / short-high-VR (trending) book is meant to harvest a
tradable **reversal** premium. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f`
(panel Close).*

## Data stamp

Stamp: 50 liquid US mega-caps, as-of 2026-06-30, Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-120-day Lo-MacKinlay `VR(q=5)`** — the overlapping, bias-corrected variance ratio (`m = q(W−q+1)(1−q/W)`), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the bottom 30%** (low VR, mean-reverting), **short the top 30%** (high VR, trending), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled low-vs-high books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; two-era & two-window robustness cuts; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Delisted
and de-rated names are absent — and those are exactly the names whose price paths are most
likely to have mean-reverted, so a 50-mega-cap survivor panel is if anything biased *against*
finding a reversal premium.

## The headline — long-low-VR / short-high-VR spread

Daily equal-weight bottom-30% (low VR) minus top-30% (high VR) spread (n = **4,026** days,
median 50 names/day). Cross-sectional VR(5) on the last day: median **0.991**, range
**[0.615, 1.526]**, **52%** of names below 1 (mean-reverting):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long low-VR − short high-VR)** | **−2.69 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−2.44** |
| one-sample *t* | −2.44 |
| low-VR book / high-VR book | +6.10 bps / +8.80 bps (Welch *t* = −1.05) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.61 |

The claimed edge **fails to replicate — and inverts.** The reversal story predicts a
*positive* long-low/short-high spread (mean-reverters out-earn); on this mega-cap universe the
spread is **significantly negative** (−2.69 bps/day, NW *t* = −2.44): the **high-VR (trending)**
names actually *out-earned* the mean-reverters over 2010–2026. These are the momentum tech
mega-caps whose trends kept paying — the opposite of a reversal premium.

## Placebo — is the (reversed) relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-VR sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−2.69 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.095 bps (0.937) |
| position of observed | ≈ **2.88σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 0.999 ⇒ left-tail p ≈ 0.001) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed −2.69 bps sits well into the **left** tail,
so the (opposite-sign) relation is not a lucky sort — the sign is simply the reverse of the
reversal story's on this universe.

## Robustness — two eras and two windows

| cut | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,892) | −3.04 bps | **−2.42** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −2.39 bps | −1.36 |
| trailing window 63d (q=5) | −0.68 bps | −0.66 |
| trailing window 252d (q=5) | −0.57 bps | −0.53 |

The wrong-sign spread reaches |*t*| ≥ 2 **only** at the 120-day window in the **early** era; the
recent era is insignificant and both a shorter and a longer VR window collapse to noise. So even
the *reversed* result is **fragile**, not a stable structural feature — there is no robust
variance-ratio effect of *either* sign to trade here.

## The timer — can you get paid for it (even the reversed book)?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −2.69 bps | 2.14 bps | **−4.83 bps** | −4.38 | −1.10 | −12.2%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −2.69 bps | 10.14 bps | **−12.83 bps** | −11.64 | −2.91 | −32.3%/yr |

The specified book loses money gross; and even the *sign-flipped* book (long high-VR) would earn
only +2.69 bps/day gross, which the 2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at a mere 1 bp one-way
already eats most of, dying entirely at any realistic cost. **Mirage** either way.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel: each name gets a fixed MA(1) coefficient (so its trailing VR is a
clean function of a latent tilt) and, with `edge>0`, the mean-reverting (low-VR) names are paid a
premium. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.05** (sd 0.83), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** (≈ nominal 5%) |
| planted (`edge = 0.0006`, seed 815) | **+9.75** (Welch *t* = +8.76) |

The detector recovers a *planted* low-VR reversal premium cleanly and essentially never fires on
the null — so the negative, fragile real-tape result is a genuine absence of the effect, not a
bug. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The famous Lo-MacKinlay variance-ratio reversal does **not** pay on 50
  liquid US mega-caps. The specified long-low-VR / short-high-VR spread is **−2.69 bps/day**
  (NW *t* = **−2.44**) — significant at the headline window but *opposite in sign* to the claim
  (the trending high-VR names out-earned), and **fragile**: insignificant in 2018–2026
  (*t* = −1.36) and vanishing at 63-day / 252-day windows (*t* = −0.66 / −0.53). A clean 20-seed
  synthetic control recovers a *planted* premium (*t* = +9.75), so the engine is sound. The
  claimed reversal edge is absent.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The specified book loses money gross and net (−4.83 bps/day at 1 bp,
  −12.83 at 5 bps); even the data-mined sign-flip is eaten by the round-trip friction at 1 bp.
